questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders carboxylic acid derivatives in order of decreasing reactivity toward nucleophilic acyl substitution?

options.label: A
options.text: Acyl chloride > Ester > Acid anhydride > Amide

options.label: B
options.text: Ester > Amide > Acid anhydride > Acyl chloride

options.label: C
options.text: Acyl chloride > Acid anhydride > Ester > Amide

options.label: D
options.text: Amide > Ester > Acid anhydride > Acyl chloride

questions.correct_answer: Acyl chloride > Acid anhydride > Ester > Amide
questions.explanation: Reactivity follows leaving group ability: Cl- > RCOO- > RO- > NH2-.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.topic: Amide vs ester vs acid chloride resonance stabilization
questions.question: Which carboxylic derivative has the greatest resonance stabilization of its carbonyl group?

options.label: A
options.text: Acid anhydride

options.label: B
options.text: Acyl chloride

options.label: C
options.text: Ester

options.label: D
options.text: Amide (strong nitrogen lone-pair donation)

questions.correct_answer: Amide (strong nitrogen lone-pair donation)
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen and chlorine, donating its lone pair extensively into the carbonyl pi system.

questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders methyl esters in increasing order of saponification rate with aqueous NaOH?

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.topic: Leaving group ability in acyl substitution
questions.question: Which ranking correctly orders leaving groups in decreasing order of leaving ability?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethoxide > Amide ion > Acetate > Chloride

options.label: B
options.text: Amide ion > Ethoxide > Acetate > Chloride

options.label: C
options.text: Chloride (Cl-) > Acetate (CH3COO-) > Ethoxide (CH3CH2O-) > Amide ion (NH2-)

options.label: D
options.text: Acetate > Chloride > Ethoxide > Amide ion

questions.correct_answer: Chloride (Cl-) > Acetate (CH3COO-) > Ethoxide (CH3CH2O-) > Amide ion (NH2-)

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Why are acid anhydrides more reactive than esters toward nucleophilic attack?

options.label: A
options.text: Carboxylate is a better leaving group than alkoxide due to resonance delocalization

options.label: B
options.text: Esters have weaker C-O bonds than anhydrides

options.label: C
options.text: Anhydrides have less steric hindrance than esters

options.label: D
options.text: Anhydrides are insoluble in water

questions.correct_answer: Carboxylate is a better leaving group than alkoxide due to resonance delocalization

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Where do thioesters (like Acetyl-CoA) rank in reactivity relative to oxygen esters and acid anhydrides?

options.label: A
options.text: Identical in reactivity to dialkyl esters

options.label: B
options.text: More reactive than oxygen esters, less reactive than acid anhydrides

options.label: C
options.text: More reactive than acyl chlorides

options.label: D
options.text: Less reactive than amides
